rel: Sir Syed also founded the Muhammadan Educational Conference in 1886.

question: When was Major Aziz Bhatti martyred?
why: Major Raja Aziz Bhatti was martyred on 12 September 1965 on the BRB Canal near Lahore and received the Nishan-e-Haider.
rel: 6 September is observed as Defence Day in Pakistan.

question: Which is considered the world's oldest sport?
why: Wrestling is generally considered the oldest sport; cave drawings of it are thousands of years old.
rel: Polo is called the 'game of kings'.

question: How many founding member countries did the UN have in 1945?
why: The UN started with 51 original members in 1945 (50 signed in San Francisco and Poland signed later).
rel: The UN Charter came into force on 24 October 1945, now celebrated as UN Day.

question: What form of government did the 1956 Constitution of Pakistan provide?
why: The 1956 Constitution gave Pakistan a parliamentary system with the Prime Minister as head of government.
rel: The 1962 Constitution introduced a presidential system.

question: What is the synonym of 'Indifference'?
why: 'Indifference' means not caring or having no interest.
rel: The adjective form is 'indifferent'.

question: When did Pakistan become a full member of the SCO?
why: Pakistan and India became full SCO members at the Astana summit on 9 June 2017.
rel: The SCO was founded in Shanghai on 15 June 2001.

question: The 1956 Constitution of Pakistan set up which system of government?
why: The 1956 Constitution was parliamentary; the presidential system came with the 1962 Constitution.
rel: Iskander Mirza became Pakistan's first President under the 1956 Constitution.
note: Notes said 'Presidential'; 1956 was parliamentary (the 1962 Constitution was presidential).

question: What is the range of the Hatf-1 missile?
why: Hatf-1 is a short-range battlefield missile with a range of about 70 km.
rel: Shaheen-III has a range of about 2,750 km.

question: How many articles are in the 1973 Constitution of Pakistan?
why: The 1973 Constitution has 280 articles. The 1956 Constitution had 234 and the 1962 one had 250.
rel: The Constitution also has a Preamble and several schedules.

question: Which article of the 1973 Constitution gives the right to education?
why: Article 25A, added by the 18th Amendment (2010), makes free and compulsory education for children aged 5-16 a right.
rel: Article 19A gives the right to information.

question: What is the synonym of 'Zeal'?
why: 'Zeal' means great energy or enthusiasm, the same as passion.
rel: A person full of zeal is called 'zealous'.

question: Khanpur Dam is built on which river?
why: Khanpur Dam near Haripur is on the Haro River and supplies water to Islamabad and Rawalpindi.
rel: Rawal Dam is built on the Korang River.

question: Which is described in the notes as Pakistan's second highest civil award?
why: The notes give Hilal-i-Imtiaz, which comes after the Nishan-i-Imtiaz for services to the country.
rel: Pakistan's highest civil award is the Nishan-e-Pakistan.
note: Sources differ: many list Hilal-e-Pakistan as the second highest civil award. Kept printed answer.

question: Where is the headquarters of the IMF?
why: The International Monetary Fund is based in Washington D.C., USA.
rel: The World Bank is also headquartered in Washington D.C.

question: Who wrote 'Humayun Nama'?
why: 'Humayun Nama' was written by Gulbadan Begum, Humayun's sister and Babur's daughter.
rel: Abul Fazl wrote 'Akbar Nama'.

question: Who wrote the Punjabi folk tale 'Sohni Mahiwal'?
why: The famous Punjabi qissa 'Sohni Mahiwal' was written by Fazal Shah. Waris Shah wrote 'Heer Ranjha'.
rel: Hashim Shah wrote 'Sassi Punnun'.

question: In which year was the first Cricket World Cup held?
why: The first Cricket World Cup was played in England in 1975 and won by the West Indies.
rel: Pakistan won the World Cup in 1992.

question: When did the USA invade Iraq?
why: The US-led invasion of Iraq began on 20 March 2003.
rel: 7 October 2001 is when the US invaded Afghanistan; 2 August 1990 is when Iraq invaded Kuwait.

question: Who wrote the novel 'Ice Candy Man'?
why: 'Ice Candy Man' (1988), about Partition in Lahore, was written by Bapsi Sidhwa.
rel: The novel was made into the film 'Earth' (1998).
